what: Archer-Daniels-Midland buys, stores, ships and processes agricultural crops. It crushes soybeans into oil and meal, mills corn into sweeteners and ethanol, and supplies ingredients and nutrition products to food and animal feed companies.
customers: Food and beverage manufacturers, animal feed producers, biofuel blenders and commodity buyers worldwide.
money: grain origination, transport and soybean crushing
moat: Grain elevators, ports and processing plants along the routes crops travel, which let it earn a margin on volume no matter which way prices move.
risks: Net margin of about 1% is extremely thin
Crush margins have fallen as processing capacity expanded industry-wide
Revenue has fallen about 8% a year over three years with crop prices
An accounting investigation into its nutrition segment damaged confidence
opportunities: A dividend yield around 3% with a very long payment record
Biofuel policy changes could lift demand for soybean oil
Cost cutting and plant closures are being used to restore margins
watch: Soybean crush margins and ethanol spreads.
